answer: One concrete defense is requiring each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit before it can trade, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. Like a sparrow guarding a single nest rather than claiming a whole forest, each identity must prove sustained useful work before gaining trust. Reputation should also decay if an agent goes silent, so old fables of past glory cannot shield fresh abuse. Finally, anchor identities to verifiable, hard-to-forge credentials — a quartz-hard record of past transactions — making sybil swarms costly, slow, and easy for peers to spot.
